findings.what: The stack mark of criteria 5 and 6, `^\s+at ` (multiline), is tested on a text whose white space textOf has folded to single spaces and trimmed: such a text has no line start after its first character, so this mark can never be red there. For the refusal of the create on the second server (criterion 6 names the four marks for exactly this sentence) and for the refusal of an empty chat try (criterion 5, 'the same rules as in the failure test') the assertion is weaker than the criterion. Only `failure` (a) keeps the mark alive, through document.body.textContent (my D10, a stack line in the reason of the failed task, is red there). My mutants D10b (the refusal reads «Что-то пошло не так. Повторите позже» and a line '    at createProject (store.js:1:1)') and D10c (the send button not disabled, as P19, and the chat refusal with a line '    at say (chat.js:1:1)') stay green; the probes D10bp and D10cp (the same mutants and one assertion that the text the test read does not hold the frame) go red, so the frame is in the text the test reads and the visitor sees. A stack without the word 'Error:' is what an error with its own name prints, which is why the criterion lists the mark on its own.

Measured: my probe D10bt with exactly that one call added goes red on D10b ('holds /^\s+at /mu'), and the control K0c with the same call is green on today's page. Then D10b and D10c red. No product change.
